name: @ocelli/oracle
description: Headless cornerstone3D reference renderer over the golden corpus (F-010, HLD section 11).
$pins: Every version here is exact, with no caret and no tilde, for HLD 15.2's reason applied to the reference rather than to wgpu: an oracle that drifts is not an oracle.
The pin is 5.8.2 and not Appendix B's v5.8.9, which does not exist. That is deviation D-11.

@cornerstonejs/tools is pinned and is NEVER LOADED by this harness. It is here because the parity target names it and because D-11 pins all three cornerstone3D packages together, so `bin/ocelli.sh oracle` refuses a tree where the version of any of them has moved. @kitware/vtk.js, gl-matrix, d3-array and d3-interpolate are its peer dependencies and are pinned for the same reason.

@cornerstonejs/codec-* are declared even though nothing here imports them by name at run time. build-page.mjs resolves them to copy their .wasm binaries into the page, and those binaries decide the decoded pixels for every JPEG, JPEG-LS, JPEG 2000 and HTJ2K row. Relying on npm hoisting them out of dicom-image-loader's subtree would make the decoders a phantom dependency, which is the one thing hoisting can stop providing without warning.
dicom-parser reads the sidecar's DICOM attributes independently of the render path, so it is pinned and version-checked too. See PINNED in run.mjs.

esbuild is not part of the reference. It is what turns the reference into a page a browser can load, and a bundler that changed the module graph between two runs would move the output for a reason nobody could see.

scripts.test: node --test tests/args_test.mjs tests/manifest_test.mjs tests/output_test.mjs tests/params_test.mjs tests/paths_test.mjs tests/pins_test.mjs tests/registration_test.mjs tests/server_test.mjs tests/sidecar_test.mjs tests/unsupported_test.mjs
